items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: I heard the Andrews Sisters and that music, so I kind of had a predisposition for that era already.

ctx.x: Did you have any memorable moments, epiphanies or aha! moments as a kid that set you on this path?

It was immediate. So — I began playing clarinet when I was ten years old in the fifth grade band. And I enjoyed swing music prior to that ‘cause I like old movies. I used to watch Abbott and Costello and I heard the Andrews Sisters and that music, so I kind of had a predisposition for that era already. And then fifth grade came along and you can join the band if you wanted to. And my grandfather just said to me, “I think you’d have fun with a clarinet.” Why he said that I don’t know. I think it was just divine…

could or couldn’t. I didn’t know anything about the possibilities of a career failing or succeeding, I just knew that something really clicked. My life felt complete. And I learned a song by ear I think within the first week or two and I just moved my fingers around. I remember “I’ll be With You in Apple Blossom Time,” I just moved my fingers and I could play that melody. And so my teacher at the time, Jamie McLeod, who is a very dear friend of mine to this day, he was I think 26 and he played clarinet too,…
